title: RouterBench: A Benchmark for Multi-LLM Routing System
benchmarks: RouterBench (405k inference outcomes over standard benchmarks)
summary: Introduces a standardized evaluation framework and a dataset of over 405k precomputed inference outcomes from a pool of LLMs so routers can be compared without re-running models. It also gives a theoretical framing of routing as navigating a cost-quality convex hull and benchmarks several routing approaches. Released by Martian.
key_idea: Precomputed multi-LLM outcome dataset plus cost-quality hull metrics for comparing routers offline.
relevance_rationale: Seed benchmark for query-level cost-aware routing; the de facto offline testbed.

title: RouterEval: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Routing LLMs to Explore Model-level Scaling Up in LLMs
summary: A router benchmark built from more than 200 million performance records spanning 12 evaluations and over 8,500 LLMs, framing routing as m-way classification over candidate pools of varying size and strength. The authors report a model-level scaling effect where a capable router improves as candidate count grows, and find most existing routers leave large headroom.
key_idea: Very large candidate pools reveal router scaling and headroom.
relevance_rationale: Seed routing benchmark; quality-focused rather than cost-focused but reusable for cost-aware studies.

title: CARROT: A Cost Aware Rate Optimal Router
benchmarks: SPROUT (GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro, MATH, OpenHermes, RAGBench)
models_studied: 13 SOTA LLMs incl. GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, o3-mini (per SPROUT)
summary: Gives a minimax analysis of routing and shows a router that separately estimates each model's cost and accuracy can be minimax optimal; proposes CARROT on that basis. Also releases SPROUT (Smart Price-aware ROUTing), an instruction-style routing dataset with chat templates and LLM-judged outcomes across current frontier and open models.
key_idea: Predict cost and accuracy per model and plug into a cost-weighted objective; SPROUT dataset for price-aware routing.
relevance_rationale: Contains the SPROUT seed benchmark and a theoretically grounded cost-aware router.

title: RouterArena: An Open Platform for Comprehensive Comparison of LLM Routers
summary: Proposes an open platform and leaderboard for comparing LLM routers, with a dataset stratified by domain and difficulty, a broad set of metrics including cost, and automated leaderboard updates.
key_idea: Standardized router leaderboard analogous to model leaderboards.
relevance_rationale: Direct cost-aware router evaluation infrastructure.
found_via: web search: RouterEval benchmark routing LLMs

title: LLMRouterBench: A Massive Benchmark and Unified Framework for LLM Routing
summary: Unified benchmark and framework with 400K+ instances over 21 datasets and 33 models, supporting both performance-only and performance-cost routing. Re-evaluating the field, it finds many routers perform similarly, several recent and commercial routers fail to reliably beat a simple baseline, and the oracle gap is dominated by model-recall failures; larger pools give diminishing returns versus curation.
key_idea: Unified re-evaluation shows most routers, including commercial ones, barely beat simple baselines.
relevance_rationale: Critical, rigorous evaluation of cost-aware routing claims including commercial routers.
found_via: web search: RouterEval benchmark routing LLMs

title: EmbedLLM: Learning Compact Representations of Large Language Models
summary: Learns compact vector representations of LLMs with an encoder-decoder trained on model-by-question correctness, then uses them for correctness forecasting, routing, and predicting benchmark accuracy without extra inference. Reports better routing accuracy and latency than prior methods.
key_idea: Model embeddings from correctness matrices enable cheap routing and performance prediction.
relevance_rationale: Seed; reusable representation for routing and offline performance prediction.

title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
summary: Benchmark of multi-turn conversations between an LLM-simulated user and a tool-using agent bound by domain policies, graded by comparing the final database state to an annotated goal. Introduces the pass^k metric for consistency across repeated trials; gpt-4o succeeds on under 50% of tasks and pass^8 falls below 25% in retail.
key_idea: pass^k exposes reliability gaps that pass@1 hides in customer-service agents.
relevance_rationale: Seed; the standard enterprise-style agent benchmark and origin of pass^k reliability metric.

title: τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
summary: Extends τ-bench to dual-control settings where the simulated user also acts on a shared environment, modeled as a Dec-POMDP, with a new telecom technical-support domain, a compositional task generator, and a tool-constrained user simulator. Agents drop sharply when moving from no-user to dual-control modes.
key_idea: Dual-control user-agent tasks for technical support.
relevance_rationale: Directly relevant to IT/tech-support agents; used by later routing evaluations.

title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
cost_reduction_reported: Reports ~$40,000 total cost for 21,730 rollouts across 9 models x 9 benchmarks; finds higher reasoning effort reduced accuracy in most runs
benchmarks: 9 benchmarks incl. coding, web navigation, science, customer service (e.g., tau-bench, GAIA, SWE-bench)
summary: The Holistic Agent Leaderboard provides a standardized parallel evaluation harness, a three-way analysis over models, scaffolds and benchmarks with cost reported alongside accuracy, and LLM-aided inspection of logs that surfaces shortcut behaviors. All 2.5B tokens of logs are released; a public cost-aware leaderboard is at hal.cs.princeton.edu.
key_idea: Cost-aware, third-party agent leaderboard with Pareto reporting and shared logs.
relevance_rationale: Seed; the main cost-accuracy Pareto leaderboard for agents.

title: AI Agents That Matter
cost_reduction_reported: Simple baselines (retry, warming, escalation) Pareto-dominate complex SOTA agents on HumanEval at much lower cost (secondary source reports ~50x)
summary: Argues agent benchmarks over-focus on accuracy, and that jointly plotting cost and accuracy shows simple baselines Pareto-dominate complex agents. Also separates model-developer from downstream-developer benchmarking needs, flags weak holdout sets, and calls for standardization and reproducibility.
key_idea: Evaluate agents on the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier, not accuracy alone.
relevance_rationale: Foundational argument for cost-aware agent evaluation; escalation baseline is a cascade.
found_via: web search: AI Agents That Matter cost accuracy Pareto

title: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
summary: A remote-hosted benchmark of 33 knowledge-work tasks on the ServiceNow platform, with certifiable oracles and validators, plus the BrowserGym environment for designing and evaluating web agents. Agents show promise but a large gap to full automation remains, especially for open models.
key_idea: Enterprise ITSM-platform web-agent benchmark with verifiable tasks.
relevance_rationale: Seed; directly the enterprise/ITSM workflow setting of interest.

title: WorkArena++: Towards Compositional Planning and Reasoning-based Common Knowledge Work Tasks
summary: Adds 682 compositional workflows on ServiceNow that need planning, arithmetic and logical reasoning, retrieval and context understanding, and compares agents with human workers. It also provides a mechanism to generate large numbers of ground-truth observation/action traces for fine-tuning.
key_idea: Harder compositional enterprise workflows plus trace generation for training.
relevance_rationale: Seed; ServiceNow enterprise workflows and trace data usable for distillation to smaller agents.

title: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research
benchmarks: 6 web-agent benchmarks unified in BrowserGym (incl. WorkArena)
summary: Unifies web-agent benchmarks under a gym-like interface and adds AgentLab for building, running and analyzing agents with reproducibility and a leaderboard. Runs a large multi-benchmark comparison of six LLMs across six benchmarks.
key_idea: Common harness for comparing web agents across benchmarks.
relevance_rationale: Evaluation infrastructure for enterprise web agents; enables controlled model-swap cost studies.

title: CRMArena: Understanding the Capacity of LLM Agents to Perform Professional CRM Tasks in Realistic Environments
summary: Benchmark of professional CRM tasks in a realistic Salesforce-like environment designed with CRM experts. Agents struggle to complete tasks reliably even with function calling.
key_idea: Realistic CRM tasks for agent evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise workflow benchmark.

title: CRMArena-Pro: Holistic Assessment of LLM Agents Across Diverse Business Scenarios and Interactions
cost_reduction_reported: Top agents ~58% single-turn and ~35% multi-turn success
summary: Expands CRMArena to 19 expert-validated sales, service and CPQ tasks in B2B and B2C settings, with persona-driven multi-turn interactions and confidentiality tests. Top agents reach about 58% single-turn and about 35% multi-turn success, and show almost no confidentiality awareness.
key_idea: Multi-turn enterprise CRM evaluation with confidentiality checks.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise agent benchmark; multi-turn drop matters for per-step model assignment.

title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
summary: Simulated small software company with internal websites, data and simulated coworkers, where agents browse, code, run programs and communicate. The best baseline agent completes 30% of tasks autonomously.
key_idea: Digital-worker benchmark with consequential multi-tool tasks.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise-like long-horizon digital-worker tasks.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
summary: Multi-environment benchmark of LLMs acting as agents in eight interactive settings, testing reasoning and decision-making. Commercial models lead, with a large gap to open models, often due to weak long-horizon planning and instruction following.
key_idea: Broad multi-environment agent capability benchmark.
relevance_rationale: Seed; background capability benchmark without cost focus.

title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM agents
summary: Benchmark for LLM multi-agent systems that measures task completion and the quality of collaboration and competition via milestone-based KPIs, across coordination topologies (star, chain, tree, graph) and strategies like group discussion and cognitive planning. gpt-4o-mini achieves the best average task score, and graph topology works best in research scenarios.
key_idea: Evaluate multi-agent topologies and coordination, not just outcomes.
relevance_rationale: Useful for judging when multi-agent structure pays off.

title: BrowseComp: A Simple Yet Challenging Benchmark for Browsing Agents
summary: OpenAI benchmark of 1,266 hard-to-find, entangled questions whose short answers are easy to verify, testing persistent and creative web browsing. Non-browsing models score near zero while an agent trained for browsing does much better.
key_idea: Short-answer verifiable benchmark for deep browsing agents.
relevance_rationale: Used in multi-agent research-system cost analyses (e.g., token usage explains variance).

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
summary: A controllable world of 9 everyday apps with 457 APIs and about 100 simulated users, and a benchmark of 750 tasks requiring interactive code generation, graded by state-based tests that also detect collateral damage. GPT-4o solves about 49% of normal and 30% of challenge tasks.
key_idea: API-rich simulated app world with collateral-damage checks.
relevance_rationale: Tool-use agent benchmark used in agent-efficiency studies.

title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
summary: Scalable real-computer environment across Ubuntu, Windows and macOS with 369 open-ended tasks and execution-based evaluation. Humans complete over 72% of tasks versus about 12% for the best model at release.
key_idea: Real OS environment for computer-use agents.
relevance_rationale: Background computer-use benchmark; used in reliability studies.

title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
summary: Benchmark of real-world assistant questions that are simple for humans but need reasoning, multimodality, browsing and tool use; humans score 92% versus 15% for GPT-4 with plugins at release.
key_idea: Human-easy, AI-hard assistant tasks.
relevance_rationale: Common agent benchmark used for cost-of-pass efficiency studies.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
summary: Self-hostable realistic web environment with sites for e-commerce, forums, code collaboration and CMS, plus tools and knowledge resources, and 812 long-horizon tasks checked for functional correctness.
key_idea: Reproducible realistic websites for agent evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Background; used in routing evaluation studies.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
summary: Benchmark of 2,294 real GitHub issues and pull requests across 12 Python repositories, requiring multi-file edits validated by tests. At release the best model solved 1.96% of issues.
key_idea: Real repository issue resolution as a coding-agent benchmark.
relevance_rationale: Background; basis for many later cost-per-task analyses of coding agents.

title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
summary: Curated set of 89 hard command-line tasks, each with its own container environment, human-written solution and tests, spanning software engineering, ML, security, sysadmin and data science. Frontier agents score below 65%.
key_idea: Hard, verified terminal tasks for agents.
relevance_rationale: Background agent benchmark.

title: WorkBench: a Benchmark Dataset for Agents in a Realistic Workplace Setting
summary: Workplace sandbox with five databases, 26 tools and 690 tasks such as emailing and scheduling, graded by unique database outcomes. ReAct agents completed between 3% and 43% of tasks and sometimes took harmful wrong actions.
key_idea: Outcome-based workplace task evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise-style benchmark.

title: Cost-of-Pass: An Economic Framework for Evaluating Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Frontier cost-of-pass for complex quantitative tasks roughly halved every few months over the year studied
benchmarks: basic quantitative, knowledge-intensive and complex quantitative task suites
summary: Defines cost-of-pass, the expected dollar cost to get one correct answer, and a frontier cost-of-pass across models and human experts, grounded in production theory. Finds lightweight models are most cost-efficient for basic quantitative tasks, large models for knowledge tasks, and reasoning models for hard quantitative problems.
key_idea: Expected cost per correct solution as a unified cost-quality metric.
relevance_rationale: A clean metric for cost-aware evaluation of routing and agent configurations.

title: ITBench: Evaluating AI Agents across Diverse Real-World IT Automation Tasks
summary: IBM framework for benchmarking agents on 94 real-world IT automation scenarios across site reliability engineering, security compliance and FinOps, with push-button workflows and interpretable metrics. SOTA agents solve 13.8% of SRE, 25.2% of CISO and 0% of FinOps scenarios.
key_idea: IT-operations automation benchmark.
relevance_rationale: Close to ITSM/IT operations enterprise workloads.

title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
summary: Proposes twelve metrics that break agent reliability into consistency, robustness, predictability and safety, borrowing from safety-critical engineering, and shows single success rates hide operational flaws.
key_idea: Multi-dimensional reliability profile beyond accuracy.
relevance_rationale: Reliability metrics needed to validate cheaper configurations.

title: Beyond pass@1: A Reliability Science Framework for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Shows that capability (single-attempt success) and reliability (consistent repeated success) diverge as task duration grows, and proposes reliability decay curves, variance amplification, graceful degradation and meltdown-onset metrics over 23,392 episodes.
key_idea: Reliability decays with horizon length in ways pass@1 misses.
relevance_rationale: Reliability measurement for long-horizon agents.

title: On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents
summary: Studies why computer-use agents that succeed once fail on repeats, attributing unreliability to execution stochasticity, task ambiguity and behavior variability, using pass^k and paired tests over repeated OSWorld runs.
key_idea: Repeated-execution evaluation for computer-use agents.
relevance_rationale: Reliability methodology relevant to validating model swaps.

title: Consistency as a Testable Property: Statistical Methods to Evaluate AI Agent Reliability
summary: Develops a statistical measurement framework for agent consistency under meaning-preserving perturbations, using U-statistics for outputs and kernel metrics for trajectories, and shows high accuracy can hide severe consistency failures.
key_idea: Statistical tests for agent consistency.
relevance_rationale: Reliability evaluation methodology.

title: Beyond Pass@k: Measuring Reliability and Security of Agentic Code Generation
summary: Shows coding-agent leaderboards misapply the pass@k estimator by counting unit tests rather than independent rollouts, and proposes reliability@k; the misapplied metric inflates scores substantially in a synthetic benchmark.
key_idea: Correct pass@k over independent rollouts.
relevance_rationale: Metric correctness for reliability claims.

title: Beyond Accuracy: A Multi-Dimensional Framework for Evaluating Enterprise Agentic AI Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Accuracy-only optimization yields agents 4.4-10.8x more expensive than cost-aware alternatives with comparable performance on 300 enterprise tasks
summary: Identifies missing cost control, weak reliability measurement (60% single-run versus 25% eight-run consistency) and missing security/latency/compliance metrics in agent benchmarks, and proposes the CLEAR framework. Expert ratings suggest CLEAR predicts production success better than accuracy alone (ρ=0.83 vs 0.41). Single-author preprint; treat numbers with caution.
key_idea: Enterprise agent evaluation on cost, latency, efficacy, assurance, reliability.
relevance_rationale: Directly argues for cost-aware enterprise agent evaluation.
found_via: web search: enterprise agent benchmark cost efficiency CLEAR

title: Efficient Benchmarking of AI Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Mid-difficulty task filter cuts evaluation tasks by 44-70% while preserving rank fidelity
summary: Finds that absolute agent scores are hard to predict under scaffold shift but rankings are stable, and proposes evaluating only tasks with 30-70% historical pass rates, cutting evaluation cost substantially while keeping rankings.
key_idea: Evaluate on mid-difficulty subsets to cut agent eval cost.
relevance_rationale: Reduces cost of evaluating candidate configurations.
found_via: web search: enterprise agent benchmark cost efficiency

title: EnterpriseClawBench: Benchmarking Agents from Real Workplace Sessions
benchmarks: EnterpriseClawBench (852 tasks from real workplace sessions)
summary: Builds 852 reproducible enterprise tasks from proprietary real workplace agent sessions, releasing the construction and evaluation protocol but not the data. The best configuration scores 0.663, and the authors argue reports must include harness-model pairing, cost and runtime.
key_idea: Benchmark mined from real enterprise agent logs.
relevance_rationale: Shows how to turn production sessions into an offline benchmark (relevant to C6).
found_via: web search: enterprise agent benchmark cost efficiency

title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
cost_reduction_reported: Issues can misestimate agent performance by up to 100% relative; ABC reduces overestimation on CVE-Bench by 33%
summary: Documents task-setup and reward-design flaws in agentic benchmarks (e.g., insufficient tests in SWE-bench Verified, empty responses counted as success in TAU-bench) and proposes the Agentic Benchmark Checklist.
key_idea: Checklist for rigorous agentic benchmarks.
relevance_rationale: Benchmark validity matters when measuring small cost-quality deltas.

title: Efficient Agents: Building Effective Agents While Reducing Cost
cost_reduction_reported: Retains 96.7% of OWL performance while reducing cost from $0.398 to $0.228 per task (28.4% better cost-of-pass) on GAIA
summary: Systematic study of efficiency versus effectiveness in agent systems on GAIA, varying backbone choice, framework modules and test-time scaling, measured with cost-of-pass. Uses the findings to build Efficient Agents, a leaner framework.
key_idea: Match agent complexity to task needs using cost-of-pass.
relevance_rationale: Direct cost reduction of agent configurations with a cost-aware metric.
found_via: web search: Efficient Agents reducing cost

title: FusionFactory: Fusing LLM Capabilities with Multi-LLM Log Data
summary: Introduces LLMFusionBench, 103M tokens of responses from 20 open LLMs over 14 tasks, and FusionFactory, which fuses models at the query level (routers), thought level (reused reasoning templates) and model level (distillation). Fusion beats the best single LLM across benchmarks.
key_idea: Mine multi-LLM logs for routing, template reuse and distillation.
relevance_rationale: Routing benchmark built from logs; bridges routing and distillation.

title: How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks
cost_reduction_reported: Agentic coding uses ~1000x more tokens than code reasoning/chat; same-task runs vary up to 30x in tokens; accuracy peaks at intermediate cost
summary: First systematic study of token consumption in agentic coding, finding input tokens dominate cost, token use is highly stochastic, and more tokens do not mean higher accuracy; also tests whether models can predict their own token cost before running.
key_idea: Characterizes and predicts agent token spend.
relevance_rationale: Grounds where agent cost comes from; informs routing and context levers.
found_via: web search: coding agents spend tokens

title: Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Three inefficient behaviors affect 79-98% of tasks and account for up to 22.75% of task cost
summary: Analyzes 1,200 coding-agent trajectories and identifies subsumed retrieval, similar-script generation and test re-execution as cost sinks, then tests mitigations over 10k trajectories, finding structure-aware retrieval can raise costs and developer-designed skills work better than agent-synthesized ones.
key_idea: Behavioral cost audit of coding agents.
relevance_rationale: Cost diagnosis methodology for agent trajectories.
found_via: web search: coding agents spend tokens

title: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction
cost_reduction_reported: Largest compression cut tool-output tokens by 38.4% but increased billed cost by 6.8%; token reduction correlated weakly with cost reduction (r=0.15)
summary: Compares token-reduction tools against unmodified Claude Code using provider-billed cost and finds prompt-cache creation and reads dominate input cost, so compression can raise cost and change trajectories.
key_idea: Measure billed cost, not tokens removed.
relevance_rationale: Important caution for cost evaluation methodology with caching.
found_via: web search: SWE-bench cost per task

title: Can your AI agent be cheaper? Investigating the effects of task specifications on token spend in agentic coding tasks
cost_reduction_reported: Bare user story vs full spec raises token spend by 29.7%
summary: Measures how task specification detail and thinking effort change agent token spend, finds task-dependent prompt sensitivity, and fits a predictor that prices spend from one cheap probe within 36%.
key_idea: Predicting agent token spend from a cheap probe.
relevance_rationale: Cost prediction is a prerequisite for budget-aware routing.
found_via: web search: SWE-bench cost per task

title: TwinRouterBench: Fast Static and Live Dynamic Evaluation for Realistic Agentic LLM Routing
summary: Step-level routing benchmark for long-horizon agents: a static track with 970 intermediate prefixes labeled with execution-verified cheapest-sufficient tiers via a downgrade-and-cascade protocol, and a dynamic track running routers live on SWE-bench Verified with realized API spend and no LLM judge.
key_idea: Benchmark for per-call routing inside agent trajectories.
relevance_rationale: Directly evaluates step-level routing in agents.
found_via: web search: agentic routing benchmark multi-turn

title: Multi-Agent Routing as Set-Valued Prediction: A WildChat Benchmark and Cost-Aware Evaluation
summary: Frames routing prompts to agents as set-valued prediction and builds a WildChat-derived benchmark with cost-aware evaluation, including a weighted routing setting over ordinal agent cost tiers. Supervised routers beat nearest-neighbor and zero-shot LLM routing.
key_idea: Cost-aware multi-label agent selection benchmark.
relevance_rationale: Evaluates subagent selection under cost; labels are heuristic.
found_via: web search: agentic routing benchmark multi-turn

title: Switchcraft: AI Model Router for Agentic Tool Calling
cost_reduction_reported: 84% lower inference cost at 82.9% accuracy (matching or exceeding best single model); >$3,600 saved per million queries
summary: Router for agentic tool calling that picks the cheapest model expected to be correct, with an evaluation framework across five function-calling benchmarks and a DistilBERT classifier under a latency budget. Finds larger models do not consistently win on tool use and cheaper models may cost more due to reasoning tokens.
key_idea: Tool-call-aware routing with corrected evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Routing specifically for agent tool calls with cost results.
found_via: web search: agentic routing benchmark multi-turn

title: Task- and Session-Level Model Routing: A Common-Interface Hybrid Evaluation of Four Open-Source Routers Across Four Benchmarks
cost_reduction_reported: No evidence of task-specific advantage over content-blind allocation for tested open-source routers
summary: Evaluates four open-source routers under a common protocol on 290 frozen tasks. Three routers emit near-constant tiers; vLLM Semantic Router varies with content but shows no task-specific gain over a share-matched blind allocation, suggesting gains track tier mix rather than routing skill.
key_idea: Controlled evaluation shows routers often just pick a tier mix.
relevance_rationale: Rigorous skeptical evaluation of production open-source routers on agent benchmarks.
found_via: web search: SPROUT cost-aware routing benchmark

title: Most of the LLM Routing Gap Is Task Type
summary: Argues most of the oracle routing gap is explained by task type, and that run-to-run noise (5.37% of model-question pairs flipping between identical runs) makes small router wins uninterpretable.
key_idea: Routing gains are mostly task-type effects plus noise.
relevance_rationale: Methodological caution for claimed routing gains.
found_via: web search: RouterEval benchmark routing LLMs

title: When Routing Collapses: On the Degenerate Convergence of LLM Routers
summary: Identifies routing collapse, where routers default to the most expensive model as budgets grow even when cheaper models suffice, attributes it to training on scalar scores rather than rankings, and proposes a ranking-based EquiRouter.
key_idea: Routers over-use strong models; learn rankings instead.
relevance_rationale: Failure mode directly relevant to cost-aware routers.
found_via: web search: SPROUT cost-aware routing benchmark

title: READY or Not: Reliable Enterprise Agent Deployment
cost_reduction_reported: Two systems 0.3 points apart in autonomous accuracy need 39.2% vs 29.6% human review to reach 76% reliability
benchmarks: clinical-audit case study (16 agent systems, 750 cases)
summary: Framework to qualify agents for enterprise deployment by measuring reliability and operating cost of the human-AI system under candidate oversight policies, selecting the cheapest policy that meets a reliability target, and statistically qualifying it on held-out cases.
key_idea: Qualify agents by min-cost oversight policy at a reliability target.
relevance_rationale: Deployment-oriented cost/reliability evaluation with deferral to humans.

title: The ML.ENERGY Benchmark: Toward Automated Inference Energy Measurement and Optimization
cost_reduction_reported: Automated optimization recommendations sometimes save more than 40% energy
summary: Benchmark suite and leaderboard for inference energy under realistic serving, with design principles and case studies on how model and serving choices affect energy.
key_idea: Energy-per-request benchmarking and leaderboard.
relevance_rationale: Efficiency leaderboard; serving cost proxy.

title: Economic Evaluation of LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: Reasoning models give better accuracy-cost trade-offs once a mistake costs more than a small dollar threshold (MATH)
summary: Proposes scoring LLMs by a single dollar-denominated number based on the use case's cost of mistakes, latency and abstention, allowing comparison beyond Pareto plots.
key_idea: Price errors, latency and abstention to compare models.
relevance_rationale: Useful objective for routing and cascade decisions.

title: ST-WebAgentBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Safety and Trustworthiness in Web Agents
summary: Enterprise-oriented web-agent benchmark scoring safety and trustworthiness under policies, with Completion-under-Policy and Risk Ratio metrics.
key_idea: Policy-compliant completion for enterprise web agents.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise evaluation dimension beyond accuracy.

title: Evaluating Test-Time Scaling of General LLM Agents
summary: Unified benchmark across agent domains and a study of sequential and parallel test-time scaling; neither axis yields consistent gains in realistic settings because of a scaling plateau and a verification gap.
key_idea: More test-time compute does not reliably help general agents.
relevance_rationale: Evidence on diminishing returns of spending more compute in agents.

title: SWE Atlas: Benchmarking Coding Agents Beyond Issue Resolution
cost_reduction_reported: Reports cost-per-task Pareto from ~$0.35/task (~15% pass) to ~$1.90/task (~40% pass) (per search-result excerpt)
benchmarks: SWE Atlas (Codebase Q&A, Test Writing, Refactoring)
summary: Coding-agent benchmark across codebase Q&A, test writing and refactoring with rubric-based quality assessment, including a cost-per-task analysis from scaffold logs.
key_idea: Coding benchmark with cost-per-task Pareto.
relevance_rationale: Cost-per-task reporting on coding agents.
found_via: web search: SWE-bench cost per task

title: Cost-Utility Alignment in LLM Agent Trajectories:Profiling,Attribution,Diagnosis,Adaptation,and Evaluation
summary: Survey-style framework treating agent trajectory cost and task contribution as dual ledgers across profiling, attribution, diagnosis, adaptation and evaluation.
key_idea: Trajectory-level cost-utility accounting.
relevance_rationale: Framework for step-level cost attribution.
found_via: web search: coding agents spend tokens

title: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
summary: Benchmark of 300 CRM tasks from user interviews on Salesforce sandboxes for computer-use agents, with milestone metrics; finds large gaps between agent paradigms and between open and closed models.
key_idea: Enterprise CRM computer-use benchmark.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise UI workflow benchmark.

title: EntWorld: A Holistic Environment and Benchmark for Verifiable Enterprise GUI Agents
benchmarks: EntWorld (1,756 tasks: CRM, ITIL, ERP, etc.)
summary: Enterprise GUI benchmark of 1,756 tasks across six domains including ITIL, generated from database schemas and verified by SQL state checks; GPT-4.1 reaches 47.61% success.
key_idea: Schema-grounded enterprise (incl. ITIL) GUI tasks.
relevance_rationale: ITIL/ITSM workflow coverage.

title: Agentic Routing: The Harness-Native Data Flywheel
cost_reduction_reported: LightGBM router preserves task quality while cutting realized cost ~90% on PinchBench and ~43% on DRACO vs fixed strong model
summary: Proposes harness-native step-level routing that picks one or several models per step using execution state, and argues routing logs form a data flywheel for training agents.
key_idea: Step-level routing inside the agent harness as a data engine.
relevance_rationale: Step-level cost reduction in agents with realized cost numbers.
found_via: web search: agentic routing benchmark multi-turn

title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
cost_reduction_reported: Blog: >85% cost reduction on MT-Bench, 45% on MMLU, 35% on GSM8K vs GPT-4 at 95% of GPT-4 quality; paper: >2x cost reduction in some cases without quality loss
summary: Trains strong/weak binary routers (matrix factorization, BERT, causal LLM, similarity-weighted) on Chatbot Arena preference data with augmentation. The LMSYS blog (lmsys.org/blog/2024-07-01-routellm) reports comparable performance to commercial routers Martian and Unify while over 40% cheaper; code in lm-sys/RouteLLM.
key_idea: Preference-data-trained strong/weak routers.
relevance_rationale: Canonical open router with blog-reported vendor comparison.

title: Arch-Router: Aligning LLM Routing with Human Preferences
summary: Katanemo proposes routing by matching queries to user-defined domain and action preferences with a 1.5B model, allowing new models to be added without retraining; it ships in the company's open-source proxy (archgw, now Plano).
key_idea: Preference-aligned routing policy model for gateways.
relevance_rationale: Router used in an open-source production gateway.

title: Building an LLM Router for High-Quality and Cost-Effective Responses
